First playthrough review time.

This game has some technical problems that affect the single player experience, but overall the campaign itself is good. The campaign is not directly available from the main game menu without going through extra steps, and players may need to restart the game several times just to access it properly. The settings option also does not work during the campaign, making it difficult to change important options like controls, sensitivity, and graphics settings.

Another major issue is that the single player campaign requires an internet connection to run. The connection to the servers can drop sometimes, forcing the player to close and restart the game. These problems affect some basic features, but once everything is working properly, the campaign provides a solid single player experience. I got this game during the Steam Summer Sale 2026 at its all time low price, mainly for the campaign itself.

Overall, the game has some technical issues, but the campaign is still a good experience. The problems can be inconvenient at times, but the game itself has a solid single player campaign.

Modern Warfare II (2022)’s campaign is a major letdown for me. The writing simply doesn’t hit the mark, and most of the characters feel like cheap knock-offs of their original counterparts. Ghost is the biggest offender here; his characterisation feels off, and he just doesn’t come across as the kind of soldier we’ve come to know from the original games.

The story itself feels all over the place, to the point where I genuinely lost track of who we were fighting and what we were even fighting for. It’s disappointing when a campaign struggles to keep you invested in its own narrative, especially when it follows in the footsteps of such iconic games.

That said, Gaz’s voice acting is genuinely great. You can tell the actor gave it his all, and his performance is one of the few highlights for me. There are also some decent set pieces throughout the campaign, but flashy action sequences can only do so much when the writing and plot fall flat.

I just wish this campaign had lived up to the standard set by the original Modern Warfare trilogy. Those games had memorable characters, gripping storytelling, and a narrative that kept you invested from beginning to end. Why does it feel like we can’t get that level of writing anymore?

Ultimately, Modern Warfare II (2022) has its moments, but the weak writing, inconsistent characterisation, and disappointing plot hold it back from being a truly great campaign.
